newsitem.title: SPAIN: Iberia says not planning fuel surcharge. [CORRECTED 16:05 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Iberia says not planning fuel surcharge. [CORRECTED 16:05 GMT]

text.p: Spain's state-owned airline Iberia said on Thursday it had no plans to levy a fuel surcharge on cargo traffic to compensate for rising jet fuel costs.
"For the time being we are not contemplating introducing a surcharge or raising rates. In January we will reasses the situation, but if we can avoid it we will," a spokesman for Iberia said.

The flag carrier said the rise in fuel prices was worrying but that the company could afford to avoid introducing a surcharge as its fuel costs had not been as bad as expected and the cargo business was doing well.
"Between January 1996 and October 1996 (corrects period) Iberia's fuel costs rose 20 percent," the spokesman said.
"Seven percent of that was attributable to the fact that we are buying more fuel and only 13 percent was down to price rises," he added.
Iberia carried 521.93 million freight tonne kilometres for the first nine months of this year or just over eight percent above the same period in 1995.

"The freight business is going very well, it's gone from being a secondary business for Iberia to a primary business," the spokesman added. "In fact we are now in a situation where we need more planes and we will be looking for at least one more plane."
The airline said it would also try to maintain passenger rates after cutting prices by up to 25 percent on a number of key trunk routes earlier this month.

Rising jet fuel prices have prompted a number of European carriers to introduce a jet fuel surcharge on cargo traffic in recent days including KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV, Swissair and Lufthansa Cargo.
The International Air Transport Association (IATA) said on Tuesday it would hold an emergency meeting on November 13 to consider "concerted action" by airlines to counter rising jet fuel costs.
